sentences.text: Today, we will talk about Moldova.
Moldova is a small, peaceful, and green country in Eastern Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Moldova?
Moldova is in Eastern Europe.
It is between Romania and Ukraine.
It is a landlocked country, which means it has no sea.
But it has hills, rivers, and fields.
What is the capital city of Moldova?
The capital city is Chishinau, say Kishinau.
Chishinau is the largest city in Moldova.
It has parks, museums, markets, and cafes.
Other towns include Baltas Tiraspol, Kahul Orhei.
How many people live in Moldova?
About 2.5 million people live in Moldova.
Many people also live and work in other countries.
Moldova has villages, towns, and a few small cities.
What language do people speak in Moldova?
The official language is Romanian.
Some people also speak Russian, Gagas, and Ukrainian.
Many young people also learn English and French in school.
What is the weather like in Moldova?
Moldova has a continental climate, warm summers, cold winters, sometimes with snow.
Spring and autumn are cool and colorful.
The weather is good for farming and vineyards.
What does Moldova look like?
Moldova has rolling hills and green fields, rivers like the Gnester River, grapevines, sunflowers and forests, villages with stone houses and gardens.
It is a very calm and green country.
What animals live in Moldova?
In Moldova you can find deer, foxes, and hedgehogs, birds like storks, owls, and ducks, cows, chickens, sheep, and goats on farms.
Dogs and cats are common pets.
Many animals live in the countryside.
What do people eat in Moldova?
Moldovan food is homemade, fresh, and delicious.

People eat bread, cheese, and eggs, potatoes, cabbage, and beans, meat, fish, and chicken, fruits like apples, plums, and grapes, popular dishes, mamaliga, cornmeal porridge, served with cheese or meat, sarmale, cabbage rolls with rice and meat, zama, chicken soup with noodles and lemon, clochinte, pastries filled with cheese, potatoes, or apples.
What do people drink in Moldova?
People drink water and fruit juice, tea and coffee, milk and herbal drinks.
Adults may drink wine.
Moldova is famous for it.
Moldovan homemade wine is shared with family and friends.
What is life like in Moldova?
Life in Moldova is simple, family -centered, and often rural.
People enjoy spending time with family, gardening, and cooking, walking in nature, going to church on Sundays, celebrating holidays with neighbors.
In cities, life is more modern with schools, offices, and shops.
What are some holidays and traditions in Moldova?
Independence Day, August 27th, Christmas celebrated in December or January.
Easter with red eggs and big meals.
Marzyshore, March 1st, the day of spring, and small red and white gifts.
Wine festivals, folk music, and dance events.
Traditional music and dance are part of many village festivals.
Some fun facts about Moldova.
Moldova is one of the least visited countries in Europe.
The Milestinich wine cellar is one of the largest in the world.
The flag is blue, yellow, and red with an eagle holding a cross.
Moldovan people are known for being kind and generous.
Many homes have gardens, and people grow their own food.
Now you know many things about Moldova.
You know where it is, what people eat, and how they live.
You learned about the land, the language, and the traditions.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emili.
